events.did: called Victor and told him they had a problem, then gave no answer when he demanded to know what it was
events.quote_anchor: “What is it?” he demanded. She didn’t answer. “June?”

events.did: dropped the phone, which fell through her fingers and struck the ground
events.quote_anchor: “June,” he snapped. Nothing. Then—a crash. The telltale clatter of the phone falling through her fingers, glass and metal striking ground.

events.did: heard footsteps over metal grating and a voice murmuring “Sweet dreams” before the call abruptly disconnected
events.quote_anchor: caught the soft echo of footsteps over metal grating, and a voice murmuring, “Sweet dreams,” followed by the scrape of the phone being lifted before the call abruptly disconnected.

events.did: concluded that EON had been transporting someone in that van whom June had mistaken for Sydney
events.quote_anchor: EON had been transporting someone in that van. Someone June had mistaken for Sydney from a distance.

events.did: identified the softer, more grown-up voice as Serena’s, whose throat he had cut
events.quote_anchor: A voice he’d never heard with his own ears because he’d stopped them up, so it couldn’t get inside his head, the night he cut its owner’s throat.

events.did: had ordered Mitch to burn Serena’s body, reasoning that crematoriums must burn at high heats
events.quote_anchor: He’d ordered Mitch to burn her body, and he had. But there was a reason crematoriums had to burn at such high heats.

events.did: recalled Sydney practicing until she needed only incomplete remains, working toward a goal and an end
events.quote_anchor: Seen her go from needing whole bodies to only incomplete remains. Not just trying to improve, he gathered now, but working toward a goal.

events.did: pushed the truck’s pedal to the floor after Victor ordered him to drive faster
events.quote_anchor: The truck whined as Mitch pushed the pedal to the floor.

relations.did: was on the phone with June when the call was cut off
relations.quote_anchor: He bristled, assuming for a moment she’d hung up on him, but when he checked, the call hadn’t disconnected.

relations.did: owned the voice Victor had stopped his ears up against, and Victor had cut her throat
relations.quote_anchor: because he’d stopped them up, so it couldn’t get inside his head, the night he cut its owner’s throat.

relations.did: was driving Victor in the truck and asked him what was going on while gripping the wheel
relations.quote_anchor: “What’s going on?” asked Mitch, gripping the wheel.

relations.did: was the one Victor expected to be easier to kill a second time
relations.quote_anchor: With any luck, Serena Clarke would be easier to kill a second time.

numbers.quote_anchor: With any luck, Serena Clarke would be easier to kill a second time.

numbers.who: the call timer on the screen
numbers.quote_anchor: The seconds continued ticking upward on the screen.

numbers.did: the only weapon she had on her
numbers.quote_anchor: And in that moment, she’d used the only weapon she had on her.
